findings.evidence: `AgreesOnIdentityComponent t u : Prop := t.realExponent = u.realExponent ∧ t.complexExponent = u.complexExponent ∧ t.complexAngularFrequency = u.complexAngularFrequency` (InfinityType/IdentityComponent.lean:37-39); the repo already destructures it positionally, e.g. `exact ⟨n, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩` at IdentityComponent.lean:84.
findings.fix: Delete the `obtain` and use `congrFun hn.1 ⟨_, hw⟩` (real case) and `congrFun hn.2.1 ⟨_, hw⟩` (complex case) to rewrite `χ.infinityType.realExponent`/`complexExponent` into `AlgebraicInfinityType.toContinuous n`'s; the `FiniteOrderInfinityType.toContinuous_*` and `add_zero` entries then drop out of both `simp only` sets.
findings.issue: `obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := (ContinuousInfinityType.agreesOnIdentityComponent_iff_exists_finiteOrderInfinityType _ _).mp hn` converts `hn` into a finite-order twist, which the subsequent `simp only [he, …, FiniteOrderInfinityType.toContinuous_realExponent, add_zero, …]` then strips back off. `AgreesOnIdentityComponent` is by definition the conjunction of the exponent equalities, so `hn` already gives them.

findings.evidence: `IsAlgebraic χ := χ.infinityType.IsAlgebraicOnIdentityComponent` (Algebraic.lean:60-61) and `IsAlgebraicOnIdentityComponent t := ∃ n : AlgebraicInfinityType K, t.AgreesOnIdentityComponent (AlgebraicInfinityType.toContinuous n)` (IdentityComponent.lean:66-68) — exactly the `⟨n, hn⟩` the two proofs reconstruct; `isAlgebraic_iff` (Algebraic.lean:65-70) is itself just that composed with the twist iff.
findings.fix: Replace both three-line blocks with `obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := hχ` (destructuring `IsAlgebraic`'s definitional existential), dropping the use of `isAlgebraic_iff` and the agreement iff in these two proofs.
findings.issue: Same re-derivation, twice: `obtain ⟨n, e, he⟩ := isAlgebraic_iff.mp hχ` followed by `(…agreesOnIdentityComponent_iff_exists_finiteOrderInfinityType _ _).mpr ⟨e, he⟩` is a round trip that lands back on the existential `hχ` already is. Repeated verbatim at lines 119-121 in `IsAlgebraic.exists_intCast_eq_shift_of_isReal`.

findings.evidence: `grep -n norm_cpow_eq_rpow_re_of_pos TauCeti/` shows the identical step at ArchimedeanCharacter.lean:125,259, InfinityType.lean:360,373, Shift.lean:92; CpowCharacter.lean (104 lines, read in full) contains only `coe_*_apply`, `*_zero`, `*_add`.
findings.fix: Add `MonoidHom.norm_coe_cpowCharacter_apply : ‖(f.cpowCharacter hf s x : ℂ)‖ = ((f x : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) ^ s.re` and the specialization `norm_coe_normCpowCharacter_apply : ‖(normCpowCharacter 𝕜 s x : ℂ)‖ = ‖(x : 𝕜)‖ ^ s.re` next to `coe_normCpowCharacter_apply`, and use them at the four new sites and in `norm_normPow_apply`.
findings.issue: `CpowCharacter.lean` has `coe_cpowCharacter_apply`/`coe_normCpowCharacter_apply` but no norm counterpart, so the step `coe_… + Complex.norm_cpow_eq_rpow_re_of_pos` is unrolled by hand at four new sites — ArchimedeanCharacter.lean:125 and :259, InfinityType.lean:360 and :373 — duplicating the existing `norm_normPow_apply` (Shift.lean:90-92), which does the same for `MonoidHom.cpowCharacter`.

summary: The purity results are genuinely new — Mathlib has no infinity-type or Hecke-character material, and no TauCeti file relates exponents to the shift. But three proofs round-trip through `agreesOnIdentityComponent_iff_exists_finiteOrderInfinityType` to re-derive what the definitions of `AgreesOnIdentityComponent` and `IsAlgebraic` already state, and the "norm of a cpow character" step is unrolled by hand at four new sites.
